items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: We fight like cats and dogs, that bitch. I’m just kidding.

ctx.x: And see how you interact with everybody, you and I think David I suspect get along pretty well.
We fight like cats and dogs, that bitch. I’m just kidding. Thank you man.

items.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: it was just Neal. Neal swung the fuck out of that band, just without a drummer.

ctx.x: By the way I’m going to ask later, I’m going to ask Neal this question, I thought I’d ask you, in a piano trio who’s responsible — is any — is the bassist or the drummer more responsible for the time?

You would naturally probably tend to say the drummer but I’ll say this. I did a big band for the hundredth anniversary of Sinatra. And we got the original Nelson Riddle charts and Count Basie charts and Sammy Cahn? No. Another one of his bands. And we had Harry Shearer, we had a bunch of artists. And it was killer. Hand picked a big band, we rehearsed. And the drummer, I’m not going to say his name, cause he’s brilliant at everything and I’m surprised that he even played big band as well. I mean you could just…
Well said. Okay. Thank you very much.
